Changes to raylib in this repository

The macOS, Windows and Android libraries are raylib 5.5 as released. The handheld library,
device/libraylib.a, is raylib 5.5 with one source file changed, and built as below.

src/platforms/rcore_desktop_sdl.c is changed so that pads plugged in after start-up, or
unplugged and plugged in again, keep working (device-pads.patch, applied to raylib 5.5). raylib
5.5 files a pad's button and axis events under SDL's instance id, which grows each time a pad
comes back, instead of under the slot it opened the pad in, and takes the removal event's
instance id for a slot. On Handtop the virtual pad comes and goes with gamepad mode, so after
leaving it once the game heard nothing from the pad. With the change each pad is found by its
instance id in the slots, a new pad goes in the first free slot, and a pad that goes away is
closed and its buttons and sticks let go.

device/libraylib.a was rebuilt with that change on 2026-11-14 with raylib's own Makefile, in an
aarch64 Debian bookworm container (GCC 12):

    make PLATFORM=PLATFORM_DESKTOP_SDL GRAPHICS=GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_ES2 \
         SDL_INCLUDE_PATH=<this repository>/third_party/sdl2/include \
         CUSTOM_CFLAGS="-DMA_NO_PULSEAUDIO -O2"

-DMA_NO_PULSEAUDIO leaves out miniaudio's PulseAudio backend, so sound goes straight to ALSA:
handhelds that run PipeWire can fail to open a playback device through its PulseAudio layer.
The library has no build folder path in it (the bundled headers are named relative to src/).
